hypotheses.mechanism: An overly aggressive learning rate causes gradient updates to overshoot optimal latent representations, resulting in unstable loss landscapes and compounding prediction errors over multi-step horizons. Reducing the learning rate dampens update magnitudes, stabilizing gradient descent and enabling the model to learn bounded latent trajectories, thereby suppressing horizon-dependent error accumulation.
hypotheses.statement: The dominant failure is optimization_instability. The exponential growth in latent MSE across prediction horizons (e+16 to e+27) and persistently low cosine similarity indicate that the optimizer is diverging due to an excessively high learning rate, preventing stable convergence of the latent dynamics predictor.
hypotheses.title: Optimization Instability Driven by Excessive Learning Rate
